differences.what: massing and placement: the three-storey red pressed-brick front, set back behind its yard, its two ground-storey round-headed lights and the round-arched door in the west bay, and the second storey's three lights over them, each where the photograph puts it (camera residuals 4.7 px RMS, about 0.12 m on the front)
the ground storey's round heads: their crowns stand about 0.25-0.3 m higher in the photograph than built, and the lights read about 0.96 m wide against the build's 0.76 m
the stone over the ground storey: the photograph's flat stone heads over the round heads read as separate blocks; the build carries them as one stone band at the same height
tone: the photograph's pressed brick is a lighter orange-red in its shade than the review render's red; the same material, read under a different light
the third storey and the cornice: out of the frame's top

the date: a 2009 photograph of the surviving house, 105 years after the scene, is evidence of 2009 (AGENTS.md rule 11); the copper's green patina, the window grilles, the fence and the planting are 2009's and are not copied into 1904

_how: verdict is unreviewed | differs | matches, set by whoever compared the side-by-side with the picture; each difference is {what, status: open | fixed | not shown | within tolerance | owner ruling} — open only if a street visitor would notice it (over about 1 ft, missing, mis-shaped, miscounted, wrong material or colour), else within tolerance (T-3153); owner ruling where the owner asked the build to depart from the picture (T-3236).
